'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**Six people are killed and two others are injured in a [[shootout]] between rival [[Drug cartel|drug cartels]] in [[Villanueva, Zacatecas|Villanueva]], [[Zacatecas]]. After the encounter, authorities arrest a suspect and decommissions five assault rifles, grenades and ammunition.[https://apnews.com/article/mexico-killings-drug-cartel-zacatecas-521c68631f44cb1a78cf90234dd903d7 (AP)] [https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/estados/mueren-6-durante-enfrentamiento-entre-grupos-delictivos-en-villanueva-zacatecas/ (El Universal)]
*[[Myanmar civil war (2021–present)|Myanmar civil war]]
**[[Operation 1027]]
***Allied rebel forces say that they have seized the town of Maw Luu in [[Sagaing Region]]. [https://www.irrawaddy.com/news/war-against-the-junta/myanmar-resistance-forces-seize-fourth-sagaing-town.html (''The Irrawaddy'')]
*[[Nigerian bandit conflict]]
**Four [[Nigerian Army|soldiers]] and two civilian drivers are killed and two [[South Korea]]n workers are [[kidnapping|kidnapped]] in an [[ambush]] against a convoy in [[Rivers State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/gunmen-kill-four-soldiers-kidnap-two-s-korean-workers-nigeria-oil-region-2023-12-13/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure (2022–present)|Russian strikes against infrastructure]]
***A [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[ballistic missile]] attack in [[Kyiv]] injures over 50 people. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/dec/13/russia-war-ukraine-strikes-kyiv-childrens-hospital-ukraine-injurie (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
**A commercial [[Tanker (ship)|tanker]], ''Ardmore Encounter'', is attacked off the coast of [[Yemen]] in the [[Red Sea]] with [[missile]]s and by gunmen using [[speedboat]]s. The ship fended off the attack and suffered no damage. Separately, the [[USS Mason (DDG-87)|USS ''Mason'']] shoots down a [[Unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drone]] launched by the [[Houthi movement|Houthis]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/gunmen-speadboat-approach-two-vessels-bab-al-mandab-strait-ambrey-2023-12-13/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Bulgaria]]n authorities begin dismantling the 45-meter-high [[Monument to the Soviet Army, Sofia|Monument to the Soviet Army]] in [[Sofia]], erected in 1954 to commemorate the [[Soviet Union]]'s [[Bulgaria during World War II#Allies|invasion of the country]] during [[World War II]]. [https://apnews.com/article/bulgaria-russia-soviet-army-monument-dismantling-sofia-5f0f21b44ad0295eabbcb588a1a7d89a (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Tesla, Inc.|Tesla]] recalls two million cars in the [[United States]] due to insufficient [[automotive safety|safety]] controls within the vehicles' [[Tesla Autopilot|AutoPilot]] system. This applies "to almost every Tesla sold in the US since the Autopilot feature was launched in 2015." Tesla will fix the issue with an automatic software update. [https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-67693935 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Sixteen people are killed in a [[multiple-vehicle collision]] on a highway near [[Caracas]], [[Venezuela]]. [https://www.nst.com.my/world/world/2023/12/990441/least-16-dead-motorway-pile-venezuela (AFP via ''NST'')]
*Five people are killed and 35 injured after a bus slid down a mountain in [[Balqa Governorate]], [[Jordan]]. [https://www.albawaba.com/news/5-killed-35-injured-bus-accident-jordan-1544964 (Al Bawaba)]
*Three people are killed and 30 injured after a water tank collapses on [[Barddhaman Junction railway station]], [[West Bengal]], [[India]]. [https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/kolkata/3-killed-30-injured-tank-collapses-west-bengal-burdwan-railway-station-9066550/?ref=archive_pg (The Indian Express)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2023 United Nations Climate Change Conference]]
**The controversial conference ends with a historic agreement urging nations to transition away from all [[fossil fuel]]s. [https://www.thedailystar.net/environment/climate-crisis/climate-action/news/dubai-summit-adopts-world-first-transition-fossil-fuels-3493431 (AFP via ''The Daily Star'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*The UK's [[Information Commissioner's Office]] imposes a [[Pound sterling|£]]350,000 ([[United States dollar|US$]]442,755) fine on the [[Ministry of Defence (United Kingdom)|Ministry of Defence]] for a [[data breach]] that exposed the [[email address]]es of 265 [[Afghans in the United Kingdom|Afghans]] seeking [[Afghan refugees|refuge]] from the [[Taliban]]. [https://mb.com.ph/2023/12/13/uk-defence-ministry-fined-for-afghan-data-breach#google_vignette (AFP via ''Manila Bulletin'')]
*[[Royal Thai Police|Thai police]] seize a record haul of [[methamphetamine]] tablets in the western province of [[Kanchanaburi]], consisting of an estimated 50 million tablets hidden in sacks in a six-wheeler truck stopped at a joint police-military checkpoint. [https://apnews.com/article/thailand-methamphetamine-smuggling-51ddf9242d7a1a9b8a151166137e0cc9 (AP)]
*A [[Colombia]]n [[Congress of Colombia|congressional committee]] orders a preliminary investigation into President [[Gustavo Petro]] over allegations of crimes in the financing of his [[election campaign]], following reports of alleged irregular campaign contributions involving his son. [https://apnews.com/article/colombia-president-petro-congress-investigatioin-f32bdce89534461af507de689eb01832 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 Pakistani protests]]
**[[Pakistan]]’s [[Supreme Court of Pakistan|top court]] allows [[military court]]s to resume the trials of more than 100 supporters of former Prime Minister [[Imran Khan]] on charges of attacking [[military installation]]s during [[Political demonstration|demonstrations]] that broke out following [[First arrest of Imran Khan|Khan’s arrest]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-court-imran-khan-trial-supporters-military-b9ed104724317dd4fc26140eac69f925 (AP)]
*[[2023 Swiss federal election]]
**[[Viola Amherd]] is elected as the [[President of Switzerland]] by the [[Federal Assembly (Switzerland)|Federal Assembly]]. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2023/12/13/swiss-name-new-president-and-cabinet-members (Reuters via ''The Star'')]
*[[Impeachment inquiry into Joe Biden]]
**The [[United States House of Representatives]] votes to formally authorize its ongoing [[Impeachment in the United States|impeachment]] inquiry into [[President of the United States|President]] [[Joe Biden]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-house-republicans-ready-vote-formalize-biden-impeachment-inquiry-2023-12-13/ (Reuters)]
*[[Donald Tusk]] is sworn in as the [[Prime Minister of Poland]], initiating [[Third Cabinet of Donald Tusk|his third cabinet]]. [https://apnews.com/article/poland-prime-minister-tusk-government-warsaw-8fd0ac25be8fee9f51ece920f493dc1f (AP)]
*[[2023–2024 Japanese slush fund scandal]]
**[[Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry|Japanese Economic Minister]] [[Yasutoshi Nishimura]], [[Minister for Internal Affairs and Communications|Internal Minister]] [[Junji Suzuki]], [[Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (Japan)|Agriculture Minister]] [[Ichiro Miyashita]], and [[Chief Cabinet Secretary]] [[Hirokazu Matsuno]] resign following a scandal involving alleged [[Kickback (bribery)|kickbacks]] within the ruling [[Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|Liberal Democratic Party]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20231214-three-japanese-ministers-resign-over-kickbacks-scandal-reports (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Mark Drakeford]] announces his resignation as [[First Minister of Wales]] and leader of [[Welsh Labour]]. A [[February–March 2024 Welsh Labour leadership election|leadership election]] will be held by the end of March 2024 to select Drakeford's replacement. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-wales-67702232 (BBC News)]
*[[2023 Indian Parliament breach]]
**Two individuals enter the [[Lok Sabha]] chamber and release a smoke canister, causing panic and adjournment of the session. The attack takes place on the 22nd anniversary of the [[2001 Indian Parliament attack]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-67700659 (BBC News)]
**15 opposition MPs are suspended by [[Vice President of India]] [[Jagdeep Dhankhar]] for 'unruly conduct' after they chanted slogans demanding a statement from the home minister [[Amit Shah]]. The suspension of one MP, [[S. R. Parthiban]], is revoked after it is revealed that he was not present in parliament for the session. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-67712325 (BBC News)][https://indianexpress.com/article/india/dmk-parthiban-lok-sabha-suspension-mistaken-identity-9068681/ (The Indian Express)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Voyager program]]
**''[[Voyager 1]]'', the farthest [[spacecraft]] from [[Earth]], launched 46 years ago, stops sending data to Earth due to a technical glitch. However, the spacecraft can still receive commands. [https://edition.cnn.com/2023/12/13/world/voyager-1-computer-issue-scn/index.html (CNN)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023–24 NBA season]]
**The [[National Basketball Association]] suspends [[Golden State Warriors]] player [[Draymond Green]] indefinitely due to Green's recurring [[unsportsmanlike conduct]]. [https://www.scmp.com/sport/basketball/article/3245000/golden-state-warriors-ace-draymond-green-suspended-indefinitely-over-nurkic-clash-says-nba (AFP via ''SCMP'')]
